page: OVHcloud rtx5000-28 is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU supports AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets but lacks hyperthreading. The server is equipped with 28 GB of RAM, providing 7 GB per core, and includes a local 400 GB SSD. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are delivered via a single NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPU based on the Turing architecture, featuring 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong capability in machine learning workloads. The server achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference speeds, processing 10592.7 tokens per second for prompts and 386.55 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M model, as well as 1854.84 tokens per second for prompts and 67.41 tokens per second for text generation using a medium 7B model. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4162.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 35.82 GB/sec falling into the bottom 25 percent. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also weak at 19.59 GB/sec, though read-only memory bandwidth for small cached blocks reaches an average tier of 353.33 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the rtx5000-28 offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of enterprise-grade data center GPUs. The dedicated CPU allocation and 16 GB VRAM make it highly suitable for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, and CUDA-based development. However, the weak multi-core CPU scaling and lower memory write speeds represent a tradeoff, making it less optimal for heavy multi-threaded CPU-bound compilation, complex physics simulations, or large-scale data decompression tasks.
